requirements.text: The system shall provide a web-based interface for managing university inventory assets including rooms, software licenses, and general equipment.
The system shall support four administrative levels: University (Level 3), Faculty (Level 2), Department (Level 1), and User (Level 0), plus an IT/Security level (Level 4).
The system shall enforce role-based access control where administrators can only manage inventory within their respective organizational scope.
The system shall allow authorized users to create, edit, modify, and transfer assets, with specific approval workflows for inter-departmental, inter-faculty, and external transfers.
The system shall support borrowing requests for assets and space reservations, requiring approval from the appropriate administrative level.
The system shall provide an authentication mechanism using username and password for all users.
The system shall allow administrators to delegate specific permissions to other users, effectively creating inventory administrators.
The system shall generate reports on assets by location, request status, and user permissions.
The system shall support bulk entry of assets via file upload.
The system shall notify users via email when their requests are processed.
Database queries shall be terminated if they exceed a execution time of 1 minute.
The system shall be designed such that the learning curve for new users is between 2 to 4 hours.
The web interface shall use consistent terminology and be accessible to users with basic internet and office software experience.
The system shall be available during university working hours, with maintenance and backups performed outside these hours.
The system shall be compatible with Microsoft and Unix platforms and support major web browsers including IE, Firefox, Chrome, Opera, and Safari.
Access to database servers shall be restricted to the IT team only.
The system shall perform periodic automated backups of all data.
The system architecture shall be designed to facilitate future evolution and ease of maintenance.
